claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in its simple solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and strength.
The low hardness and strength are governed by the absence of short-range order.
Short-range order provides local barriers to dislocation motion.
Without short-range order, dislocations glide with high mobility.
High dislocation mobility produces good ductility and machinability but low resistance to plastic deformation.
The as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
The as-cast alloy contains minimal or no short-range order.
Annealing at 600 °C for 1, 5, or 10 hours followed by rapid quenching can induce different degrees of short-range order.
The proposed annealing and quenching treatments can induce short-range order without causing secondary-phase precipitation.
Atomic-scale short-range order acts as discrete obstacles to dislocation motion.
Local chemical and structural variations associated with short-range order hinder dislocation motion.
At small plastic strains, yield strength is controlled by obstacles to dislocation slip.
Increasing short-range order without precipitation will increase hardness and yield strength relative to the as-cast alloy.
Increasing short-range order will cause only a moderate reduction in plasticity.
The as-cast baseline has high dislocation mobility and a low density of dislocation obstacles.
The proposed mechanism is limited to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state, tested at room temperature or 600 °C under quasi-static compression up to about 2–3% plastic strain.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires successful induction of measurable SRO without precipitation to test its mechanical effect, but the falsification rule also treats failure to form substantial SRO as falsification. Failure of the manipulation would make the proposed mechanism untested rather than falsified.
